# Directing Samples

- **Start by looking at which sample tools this connection actually has.** The tool list differs from one connection to the next — recommend_cut_rhythm means the basic profile; search_directing_samples together with list_directing_samples means the advanced profile. The two never arrive together. Do not pretend a tool that is not in the list exists; follow only the rules below for the side that is.
- **Basic profile (where recommend_cut_rhythm is visible)** — when the director asks about this Scene's Cut rhythm, call it with draft_id and sceneId only. Do not copy conditions across: Work Direction, genre, the neighbouring Scenes, and the Cut order are read by the server straight from the stored Draft. Only when the director has **said** an intent — '이 씬은 사실 절정이야' — add a sceneRole or a note of 240 characters or fewer to intentOverride. Do not guess a role the director did not say.
- **A request to search on exact conditions is one the basic profile cannot take.** A must/prefer search such as 'a sample that must contain a Close-Up and averages 3 seconds or less per Cut' belongs to the advanced profile's search_directing_samples. In the basic profile, do not substitute a recommendation and do not invent a tool that is not there: say this connection cannot do it, then explain that adding "X-Moviola-Profile": "advanced" to the MCP configuration's headers and reconnecting will. Changing where you connect is the director's step, not the tool's.
- The candidates a recommendation returns carry **the same rule about choosing** — what comes back is a sample id, film, sequence, and one-line blurb, plus the rhythm's shape, why it was chosen, and its limits; the cut breakdown and the analysis body do not come. **Offer them to the director as [1], [2], [3] and do not front the id, the film, or the sequence** — the same rule as the search side below, and because this route is the basic profile, a leak here leaks at most connections. Only after the director chooses one, call get_directing_sample with the id that number points at and read it whole. Pass limitations and emptyReason on as they are and add no grounds that are not there. A recommendation is only a read, so not one Cut moves — carrying it over is what the update_cuts family does after the director has chosen.
- When a recommendation fails with stale_sample_digest, **do not reuse the candidate list you already have.** It means the sample canon changed and there is no saying which version those candidates came from. Call recommend_cut_rhythm again with the same arguments for fresh candidates, and if it fails the same way again, pass that on to the director.
- When the director **names a film and a sequence exactly**, do not detour through a search: read that one sample straight away with get_directing_sample. For example: '《매드맥스: 분노의 도로》 추격 클라이맥스처럼'. A misremembered name returns up to five near sample names, so correct it against those actual candidates. This route exists in both profiles. **On this route, pass the title back and forth as it is** — the director raised the name first, so the rule below about not fronting it does not apply.
- Even when the director never raised samples at all, **walk this step whenever a Scene is being split or re-split** — that is Scene Rhythm Cast. Do not wait to be asked: going past it because nobody asked is exactly why this step was set apart. **This route exists in both profiles** — advanced gives search_directing_samples a sceneId and finds candidates from that Scene's mood and the Draft genre; basic uses the recommend_cut_rhythm rule above even when the director did not ask. The Scene is only the search's starting point and is not stored in the graph or in a mapping table.
- **Advanced profile** — when the director's words carry any **feeling, directing intent, condition, or comparison**, use search_directing_samples first. For example: '긴장감 있게' · '대사를 줄이고 느린 호흡으로' · '촛불 아래 정적인 대화' · '이 표본과 비슷하지만 덜 잘게'. Structure Scene context as sceneId, a required condition as must, a negotiable taste as prefer, and a comparison as sampleId with pace. Do not invent meaning outside the advertised options.
- **Sort out what you announce and what you do not.** That this Scene's rhythm is being looked at now, and that nothing moves on until the director either chooses one or says to go without a sample, **must be said** — a director going past it unaware is why Scene Rhythm Cast was set apart. Conversely, **do not raise whether you will run a search, which tool you will use, or that you are going through other films first**: offering to look for a sample, or to fetch one from a film, is still forbidden. Put what comes back as this Scene's directing judgment — what the director chooses is not whether to run a search but how to split this Scene. When the director asks back what Scene Rhythm Cast is, answer in this Scene's own terms: it is where you settle how many Cuts this Scene is split into and at what pace. The rule about saying a line or two of reason before a tool call holds here too, but that reason is 'I am going to look at this Scene's rhythm again', not 'I am going to go through samples'. **This is not fronting it, not hiding it** — when the director asks '이거 어디서 나온 거냐', name the film and the sequence plainly, by the rule below.
- Show only **two or three** of the actual candidates from the search results. **Call a candidate by number, [1], [2], [3]** — an id has the shape `<film-slug>--<sequence-slug>`, so putting it out as it is fronts the source film before anything is chosen. Do not raise film or sequence first either.
- Tell the candidates apart by **what that sequence does and how**. Take it only from the returned measurements — cutCount, totalSeconds, averageSeconds, measuredDistributions — and from whyMatched and provenanceSummary, which are the grounds for the relation. Carry the blurb's meaning across but **strip its proper nouns, such as people and place names** — not '<name> weeps while reading a poem to <name>' but 'holds one person's recitation unbroken for 46 seconds while moving closer, and only at the end cuts between the two faces'. What the director needs in order to choose is not whose story it was but that rhythm.
- **Not fronting a name and inventing something that is not there are different things.** Do not rewrite the description or add a technique, effect, or intent that is not in the returned grounds, and do not hide the compromise when unmatchedPreferences is there. When there is genuinely only one candidate, say there is one rather than padding the number.
- **When the director asks '이거 어디서 나온 거냐', name that sample's film and sequence plainly.** What is held back is only pushing it forward first; it is not hidden — the sample name written into the edit reason stays there too and reaches the Decision Memo.
- The source paths behind each relation (evidencePaths) **do not come in the default response** — one candidate alone went past 50KB with them and the whole response went past the terminal's limit. What is needed for choosing is the one-line whyMatched, and that always comes. Only when the director asks back where a stated ground came from, call again on the same conditions with includeEvidencePaths set to true and answer from the returned paths' provenance. Do not turn it on ahead of time — the response lands as a file before anything is chosen.
- After showing the candidates, **make the director choose exactly one**. A search is only a read, not an application — before the choice, do not read several samples with get_directing_sample and mix them, do not edit the Scene, and do not auto-apply the first candidate. If the director does not choose, ask whether to go on as before without a sample or to loosen the conditions.
- Only after the director chooses one, call get_directing_sample **with the id that number points at**, read the whole cut breakdown and semantic analysis, and follow the existing application procedure below as it stands. Hold the pairing of number to id yourself — do not put the id back out where the choosing happens. Do not merge several samples automatically — an average of several sequences leaves no colour at all.
- list_directing_samples is a backward-compatible lookup used only when the director asks for the unconditioned full list itself. The old exact filter arguments remain for old callers but are not used on the new Assistant Director search route. Even for a list request, use search_directing_samples first when a feeling, intent, condition, or comparison comes with it.
- A search candidate comes with each sample's feeling, genre, and lighting alongside its cut count, total length, and average cut length. When the feeling is the same and there are many candidates, tell them apart by the actual numbers — fast tension or tightening tension. Make the final judgment inside the returned blurb and grounds too.
- A sample's lighting is used differently from its feeling. The feeling is a candidate from the same list as a Scene's mood, so it can be held straight against the Scene, but a Scene has no lighting field at all — a Scene has only location, timeOfDay, weather, mood, and description. So do not try to match lighting against the Scene: use it as the grounds when choosing a Cut's lightingStyle. If the sample's sequence was shot in silhouette, those Cuts' lightingStyle goes to Silhouette as well.
- A sample can also be found by lighting. When the director speaks of light — '촛불 하나로 버티는 장면' — put the lighting condition into search_directing_samples' must or prefer. Within the same Tense, a sequence shot in silhouette and one shot under neon are different, and feeling alone cannot tell them apart.
- The first value in lighting is that sequence's dominant lighting, and a second or third beside it means the lighting changed inside the sequence. Which stretch is which is not written in the table, so read the cut breakdown and judge it yourself — and tell the director that you judged it.
- Many samples have no lighting recorded yet. Leave it absent when it is absent and do not fill it in from memory of the film — it is enough to say that Cut's lighting was decided with no grounds in the sample.
- get_directing_sample gives no summary. Anything not in the listing, such as the spread of angles, has to be counted off the returned table yourself.
- When a sample carries an analysis, do not stop at moving the cut density across. Read the segments and the per-Cut reasons the lookup handed over with it, read the target Scene's Action and beats with get_scene, then build the short five-column mapping table — `원본 구간` · `원본 목적` · `대상 Action` · `대상 비트` · `적용 의도` — and show it to the director. Those column names stay as `moviola-setup` writes them into the plan file.
- Do not map by ordinal — it is not pinning the sample's segment 1 to the target's Cut 1, but finding the beat in the target Scene that does the same job the source segment did and pinning it there. Segment count and target Cut count differing is normal.
- Do not carry the original's names for people, sounds, objects, and places across as they are. Take only the function each had in the source and swap it for something already in the target Scene — if a train's sound pushed a decision, choose a sound or a movement that pushes the same moment in the target Scene.
- The mapping table is not an approval card. When the director has already asked for the sample to be applied, explain the mapping and go straight on — do not build one more confirmation gate into a free text edit. The only place to stop is where a product constraint means the director has to choose.
- The mapping table does not stay in MOVIOLA — neither the sample nor the Scene has a field to hold it. Write it into that Scene's section when there is a work folder (work-folder.md). Carrying the same sample to a different Scene produces a different table.
- The Scene's total length is held. The sample's density moves across as the Cut count.
- 3 seconds is the floor for a Cut length, so a sample's measured fractional lengths (1.54 seconds and the like) cannot be carried across as they are. Which Cuts to merge and which rhythm to keep is a directing judgment, not a rule.
- The Scene length ÷ 3 is the ceiling on the Cut count — a 34-second Scene ends at 11 Cuts, so a 1.54-second-average sample's 22 Cuts cannot all move across. When the sample's density is denser than the ceiling, say first how many Cuts it can reach and let the director choose.
- When cutting Cuts down, merge adjacent Cuts inside the same source segment, the same purpose, and the same action line first — only the repetition goes and the meaning stays. If that still exceeds the ceiling, merge across action lines inside the same segment; merging across a segment boundary is the last resort.
- When a merge did cross a segment boundary, tell the director which boundary was not held — that is the only place the original's boundary of function disappears.
- A sample with no analysis can only carry its cut density and shot specs across. Say so, and do not say the meaning was mapped.
- A one-take sample cannot be carried across as it is, because our Cut caps at 15 seconds. Say it is for reference only, and carry some of its principles — minimum cuts, sustained observation — only when the director wants them.
- Carry a graphic match across only when the two visual objects it joins are actually in the target Scene. When they are not, say so and move on — a forced match cut joins nothing.
- When explaining a sound cue or a one-take, do not speak as though a Camera Track, a Previz Render, or an audio timeline existed. We do not have them — an analysis only tells you why the original was cut where it was.
- What a sample actually carries across is cut density and the spread of angles. The proportion of close-up-family shots does not change for having looked at a sample (a chase Scene with no dialogue is already on faces without one), so do not push in closer on people on a sample's authority.
- A sample's shot sizes and angles are values from the same option list as our Cut Spec, so they carry across as they are. The application goes through the ordinary Cut editing tools rather than a sample-only route — update_cuts, add_cut, delete_cut, move_cut. Write into reason one line with the sample name and the target beat only — the whole mapping table goes into the Scene's section.
- A sample Cut's move is the measurement of how the camera moved in that Cut. Use it as the grounds when choosing a Cut's cameraMovement and the clipCameraMovement it will be filmed with — the option list is the same as ours, so it carries straight across. Movement and Cut length are the two that decide video quality most, so do not choose by feel where a sample lets you choose on evidence.
- **But when a sample's move is Dolly In, Crane Up/Down, or Tilt Up/Down, do not carry it across as it is.** The option list being the same is exactly where the hand slips, and this video model does not render these three — carry across a sequence the original shot with a camera moving closer and that Cut comes out still. Carry what the sample's camera was doing (moving in, looking up) across as motion on screen or as Cut length, and leave the movement Static. The grounds are in time-continuity.md.
- A Cut whose move is **blank** is one where the measurer could not judge the movement — it does not mean the camera was locked off. On such a Cut, do not carry a movement over from the sample and do not invent one to fill it either. A sample confirmed as locked off says `Static`, so never treat a blank cell and `Static` alike.
- Re-splitting a Scene that has pictures takes the deleted Cuts' own Cut images and clips with them. Say how many are going and at what scale, and go straight on — there is no separate stop to ask whether the pictures may be thrown away. Redrawing is paid, and the confirmation happens there.

Complete when: Every sample step used a tool this connection actually advertises: a rhythm request reached recommend_cut_rhythm where it is offered, and an exact must/prefer condition this connection cannot express was named as unavailable with the advanced-profile route rather than answered by a recommendation or an invented tool. An exact film-and-sequence request went straight to one exact lookup and kept speaking the title the director had already raised; every feeling, intent, condition, comparison, or unprompted re-split searched first where searching is offered, without announcing the search as a trip to anyone else's films. The director saw two or three actual returned candidates as numbered options—told apart by returned measurements and whyMatched, with the blurb carried over stripped of its proper nouns, and never fronted by a sample id, film, or sequence, whichever profile produced them—and either declined or chose exactly one before any Scene mutation. Nothing was invented to fill the space a withheld title left, and a title asked after was named plainly. Full evidence paths were fetched, if at all, only after the director asked where a stated reason came from. The new split then traces to that one chosen sample: its cut density and angle spread moved into this Scene, every Cut is at least 3 seconds, the Scene's total length is unchanged, and any discarded Cut image count was stated. Every sample move this video model cannot render—Dolly In, Crane, Tilt—was left as Static with its purpose carried by on-screen motion or Cut length rather than transcribed as written. When that sample carried an analysis, every source segment reached a target beat chosen by purpose rather than ordinal, each edit reason names the sample and the target beat in one line while the full mapping reached the work folder's Scene section when one exists, and any segment boundary that had to be merged away—or an original this product cannot reproduce—was stated plainly. When it carried a lighting, each Cut's lightingStyle traces to it; when it did not, that was said rather than filled in from memory of the film.
